Loading Simulator for Underground Mining LHD Simulator (Load, Haul, Dump) The tender must take into account the overall implementation of the procurement in accordance with the terms and conditions set out in the invitation to tender. If the total price of one or more simulator types exceeds the estimated price set out in the invitation to tender or other procurement documentation, the contracting entity has the right not to procure the simulator type(s) in question and allocate the funds to one or more other simulator types. 4.1 Simulator The loading simulator must correspond to the functions and control devices of the equipment used in mines in Finland and Sweden to provide students with a learning experience that mirrors real working life. The simulator must have an authentic control and management system that matches the control systems of machines used in mines. The simulator should, where possible, offer performance monitoring and evaluation to support training (e.g., accuracy, efficiency, safety). The loading simulator must not have an enclosed cabin. It is considered an advantage if the simulator allows practicing various underground mining tasks, such as loading into transport vehicles and loading into ore passes, etc. Additionally, it is considered an advantage if the simulator guides the student in the correct and safe use of the machine during the scenario. 4.2 Hardware The control devices (levers, pedals, buttons, displays) must match the controls of real mining machines, and their response must be as realistic as possible. The simulator must "understand" impossible movements and machine collisions. 4.3 Software The possibility of simulating fault diagnostics and error situations (troubleshooting exercises) and scale simulation is considered an advantage. Additionally, the software should allow for monitoring learning outcomes (scenario reports from various exercises). 4.4 Displays and VR Support The simulator's display(s) must be expandable to modern display technology, enabling the creation of a realistic mining and drilling environment. A solution based solely on VR glasses is not accepted, but the possibility of using them alongside other display technology is considered an advantage. 4.5 Maintenance and Support The simulator supplier must provide sufficient user and maintenance training for the teaching staff and deliver comprehensive user manuals for the simulator and its software. Software updates and extensions must be available for at least five years. The availability of spare parts and maintenance must be ensured for long-term use. The offer must state the availability of spare parts. 4.6 Delivery The supplier is responsible for transporting the simulator to the purchaser (TOP Keskikatu 69, 95400 Tornio), including any transport insurance and agreements. Additionally, the simulator supplier commits to delivering software updates to ensure the simulator meets the requirements of the mining environment well into the future. The offer must state the software update period in years to which the supplier commits. 4.7 Other Matters The goal of the procurement is to provide mining students with work-life-oriented mining education through situations similar to a real working environment in safe and cost-effective simulated conditions and to obtain a flexible and scalable solution for mining education needs, where physical and virtual learning support each other. Additionally, the purchaser is willing to engage in other cooperation and partnership in developing mining education environments with the supplier. The procurement is made based on overall economic affordability (price scoring max 70 points, quality scoring max 30 points). Offers are also evaluated based on the overall implementation of the simulators to achieve the most functional overall solution for the educational environment, serving students, teaching staff, and industry representatives, to whom mining education provides new skilled workers. The procurement unit has the right to leave the procurement or part of the procurement unmade for a justified and valid reason. The procurement unit may leave the procurement contract unmade for one, several, or all parts of the procurement for a justified and valid reason. A justified reason may be, for example, that the budget allocated for the procurement/procurement package is exceeded, the procurement or part of the procurement becomes unnecessary, or no comparable offers have been received in the tendering competition.

Kuntien Hankintapalvelut KuHa Oy (jäljempänä Hankintayksikkö) perustaa dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän (jäljempänä DPS) aurinkovoimaloista. Hankinnassa mukana olevia Tilaajia voivat olla Kangasalan, Nokian, Oriveden ja Ylöjärven kaupungit sekä Lempäälän, Pirkkalan ja Vesilahden kunnat (jäljempänä Kehyskunnat). Tilaajia voivat olla myös edellä mainittujen kaupunkien ja kuntien tytäryhteisöt. Hankinnan kohteena ovat Kehyskuntiin toimitettavat aurinkovoimalat asennettuina sekä muut aurinkovoimaloihin liittyvät tuotteet ja palvelut, kuten suunnittelu, seurantajärjestelmät ja komponentit. Dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän keston aikana kaikki kiinnostuneet ehdokkaat tai niiden yhteenliittymät voivat hakea osallistumista järjestelmään. Hankinnat toteutetaan dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään hyväksyttyjen toimittajien kesken DPS:n Sisäisillä kilpailutuksilla, jotka voivat ajoittua dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän hankintavaiheen koko voimassaoloajalle. Järjestelmään osallistuminen ei tarkoita suoraan osallistumista kilpailutettaviin hankintoihin, vaan Ehdokkaan tulee hyväksymisen jälkeen erikseen jättää tarjous avattaviin DPS:n Sisäisiin kilpailutuksiin. DPS:n Sisäisissä kilpailutuksissa määritellään tarkemmin kulloinkin kilpailutettavien aurinkovoimaloiden yksityiskohtaiset ominaisuudet ja hankintaa koskevat ehdot. Sisäisten kilpailutusten eli kohdekohtaisten kilpailutusten kokonaistaloudellisen edullisuuden perusteet määritellään tarkemmin kutakin hankintaa koskevassa tarjouspyynnössä. Hankintasopimuskohtaiset vaatimukset, kuvaukset ja muut asiakirjat ovat nähtävillä Sisäisen kilpailutuksen avaushetkellä DPS:ään hyväksytyille Ehdokkaille. Kustakin dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän sisäisestä hankinnasta pyydetään tarjous sähköisessä kilpailutusjärjestelmässä. Hankintayksikkö hyväksyy järjestelmään kaikki osallistumishakemuksen jättäneet Ehdokkaat, jotka täyttävät Ehdokkaille asetetut soveltuvuusvaatimukset. DPS:n suunniteltu aloitusajankohta on 1.9.2024. DPS:n kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin tässä osallistumispyynnössä ja sen liitteissä.

To be considered for inclusion on a Qualification Panel(s), applicants must complete the Pre-Qualification Questionnaire (PQQ) providing relevant details in relation to the criteria set out below for assessment. It is envisaged that this qualification system will be used to either purchase and or lease during the five-year term of the Qualification System. Economic operators apply once to qualify onto the panel by providing details of their financial and technical capacity against predefined published Selection Criteria within a PQQ. The Qualification Panel for the Purchase and or Lease of Buses and Coaches will be broken down in to sub categories called Lot 1 – Purchase of Buses and Coaches Expressway, and Lot 2 – Lease of Buses and Coaches Expressway, Lot 3 - Purchase of School Buses and Coaches, Lot 4 - Lease of School Buses and Coaches, Lot 5 - Purchase of single or double deck city bus type vehicles and Lot 6 - Lease of single or double deck city bus type vehicles. Economic operators can apply for the Lot(s) that best reflect their commercial operations. Economic operators must complete a PQQ for the Lot(s) that they wish to qualify to. Only economic operators who satisfy the selection criteria of each individual Lot will qualify on to that Lot. After the initial advertisement, the panel must be advertised annually for the duration of the panel (5 years) to continually inform the market place of its existence. Economic Operators can apply to qualify on to the panel, throughout the duration of the panel. Economic Operators who are already qualified to the panel can also amend their application at any interval should their financial or technical capacity or capability change. Qualifying onto a panel does not guarantee any work and/or contracts to a supplier. There is no obligation to use the Qualification Panel and contracts can be advertised on an individual basis using the Negotiated Procedure. (Annual Readvertisement 3/8 - Amended)

All services contribute to achieve the project objectives of STREAM+ (Output 4 of SPACES II) and comprise four work packages (WP): WP 1 concentrates on mainstreaming, institutionalisation, capacity building and implementation of/for climate-resilient, sustainable and inclusive forest management (SFM+) at the local and strategic-political level, with the following main activities as i) multi-stakeholder workshops to identify solutions for climate-resilient forest use and to strengthen the role of Forest User Groups in SFM+, ii) elaboration and testing of a vertical structure concept of NFA and iii) technical advice on selected forestry policy instruments and for reporting on forest management planning, implementation and monitoring (FMPIM). Selected main results are improved legislation and policies and FMPIM reports. WP2 provides capacity building of NFA, local forest administration, PFE, FUG in planning, implementation and monitoring of SFM+ with the main activities i) advice territorial plan development working groups at local level, ii) elaborate a climate risk study related to forest management, iii) execute a gap analysis on needs of digital precision technologies, iv) improve fire management structures and approaches, v) update planning and inventory methods, v) support the development of SFM+ plans, vi) capacity building on local level regarding silviculture, improved fire management, remote sensing tools, and vii) analyse and recommend relevant actors on basic forest economic data. Selected main results are 15 elaborated and partly implemented plans for SFM+, 2.105.931 ha of forests under sustainable management and 7 local territorial development plans incorporating SFM+ principles. WP 3.a aims on strengthening sustainable inclusive forest-based value chains (VC) with Forest User Groups (FUG) and Micro-, Small- and Medium Enterprises (MSME). The focus is on timber forest products (TFP) from thinning and dead wood as well as non-timber forest products (NTFP). Main activities are i) multi-stakeholder roundtables on VC, ii) elaborate training material and conduct trainings on VC, iii) conduct studies on market opportunities, limitations, feasibilities, iv) advice national partners on the mentioned topics and v) develop recommendations for related policy instruments. Main results are a certain number of studies, capacity building measures and reinforced forestry-related VC. WP 3.b focuses on strengthening entrepreneurial and networking capacities of FUG and MSME with regard to formal markets, adding value and achieving a positive return on sustainable forest management that improves forest health and climate resilience. If feasible, synergies with national business incubator service providers and TVET shall be fostered. Main activities are i) support to selected FUG to become private entities to implement SFM+ activities, ii) a capacity-building needs assessment and relevant training for incubator service providers, iii) capacity building to FUG and MSME regarding organisational and entrepreneurial capacities, building strategic partnerships, business plans, product development, work safety and traceability systems. Main results are i) 10 FUG with a bankable business plan for forest management, ii) 3 user agreements for legal and sustainable use of TFP and NTFP and iii) 100 (green) jobs supported.
